Modern man has had too many experiences.
├── 1240853866662391810 [2020-03-20] @PrinceVogel 💜 71 🔁 1
│   Experiences teach us how to relate to the world. Portions of the world change 'tenor' as our experiences teach us about their significance. Events often have mixed significance. This becomes clear especially in extreme events, which can be a medley of good and bad.
│   ↓
│   1240853870172966912 [2020-03-20] @PrinceVogel 💜 102 🔁 6
│   Every confusing experience can make the next experience more confusing, if its value depends on the interpretation of the previous experience. If you surround yourself with intense/complicated experiences, and don't have time to process them, you just end up confused.
│   ↓
│   1240853871724879872 [2020-03-20] @PrinceVogel 💜 77 🔁 4
│   Not confused in a way facts can easily resolve. Because facts can't resolve them many people chase experiences they hope will resolve a very tangled thread and make their life "clear". This rarely works. It's better to cut down on the variety and intensity of your experiences
│   ↓
│   1240853872710569984 [2020-03-20] @PrinceVogel 💜 97 🔁 9
│   I'm not any sort of ascetic. I'm not cutting down on new experiences because I think that sex/music/movies/whatever are bad. I'm doing it so I can experience them in a "fresh" way. You get fresh experience by resolving old threads of confusion about intense experiences.
│   ↓
│   1240853885008236545 [2020-03-20] @PrinceVogel 💜 124 🔁 12
│   Despair sets in when you feel your life will never be clear. When confusion is everywhere you turn. Despair often leads to the relentless pursuit of new experiences, 'degeneracy', because people start thinking that nothing inside of them can resolve their confusion.
└── 1255181582429835265 [2020-04-28] @nosilverv 💜 3
    @PrinceVogel @dchem

1252278669189378048 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel 💜 3
A lot of what we do is a cope for not being worthy of imitation.
↓
1252278670745427968 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel 
Used to be, hero would go out into the world, conquer some chaos, become worthy of imitation, come back and be imitated. It doesn't work like that anymore. This has led to a lot of resentment on the part of people who would have been, or who have tried to be, heroes.
↓
1252278672922296329 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel 
The structure of imitation itself is breaking down. People become heroic, and the general population doesn't know where to fit in them, how to value them in comparison to everything else.In the sense of venturing into the unknown, we may in fact have a surplus of heroes.
↓
1252278674725847041 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel  [(SEED) type=quote_of_root]
But as each person brings back some esoteric knowledge or way of being, they add to a truly confusing milieu of experience. https://t.co/ln3r1Ee9Gm
  [Quoting @PrinceVogel: Modern man has had too many experiences.]
↓
1252278676802207747 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel 
Most of the most capable people I know have been crippled in some unique way, and also possessed strange abilities, drawn from all the caverns of the modern availability of information. Hard to imitate - damn near impossible.
↓
1252278678844608512 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel 
Some of the would-be heroes end up shouting about the supremacy of their virtues from the roof tops. Why discipline is best, why knowledge is best. It's as if they think the problem is that other people haven't noticed their virtues - but the problem is they've noticed too many.
↓
1252278680493060096 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel 
Others recede into quietude. A noble path, but it is not enough. The only answer, as far as I can tell, is a structure of values (Could be embodied in a person or an organization) which captures the self-evident significance of the virtues people see. One which is balanced.
↓
1252278682309148686 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel 
The would-be heroes (And I address myself most of all), need to balance out their worst faults. We need to not be like the reverse cripples. We need to balance head, and heart, and hand. https://t.co/iFJmPJmIXc
Images:
  - [Image #0] The image is a page from a book, featuring a passage of text. The transcribed text is as follows:
    
    "But this is what matters least to me since I have been among men: to see that this one lacks an eye and that one an ear and a third a leg, while there are others who have lost their tongues or their noses or their heads. I see, and have seen, what is worse, and many things so vile that I do not want to speak of everything; and
    ------------------------------------
    138
    concerning some things I do not even like to be silent: for there are human beings who lack everything, except one thing of which they have too much—human beings who are nothing but a big eye or a big mouth or a big belly or anything at all that is big. Inverse cripples I call them."
    
    The page number "138" is visible at the bottom of the page.
↓
1252278684439855108 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel 
When you bring enough virtues into harmony, many different forms of virtue will flock to you. "The people flow to the True King like water flows downwards"This stuff is near the very heart of civilization - the harmony of many different positive human ambitions.
↓
1252278686109163520 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel 
The more virtues are out of harmony, the more people depend on other forces to try to connect with others.They make money the measure of man, or force, or having the correct political doctrine. When you lose faith in trust, you go searching for chains to hold people close.
↓
1252278687862407181 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel 
If you're not receiving as much esteem, acceptance, or guidance as you think you should be - you're right. We exist in a strange jungle of a society.Find the people most worth imitating. Be well-rounded enough that your life isn't obviously missing something crucial.
↓
1252278689204547584 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel 
This means being capable of a dynamic range of behavior even if your life never calls for it. The heights of love and violence.When thinking about the virtues of others and myself, I sometimes think "What crucial behavior will this path never produce or value?"
↓
1252278690785816576 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel 💜 1
Will this person never be able to sing? Will they never be able to dance? Will they never know how to work hard, to be at true rest?The word "Never" here is doing a lot of work.It's fine to not be able to do anything of these things now.  But you should reach them eventually.
↓
1252278693252132864 [2020-04-20] @PrinceVogel 
I say this as someone who isn't very good at any of those things. But if you come to understand the limitations of your own virtues (for many,the limitations of knowledge), those very limitations tell you of the relationships between the virtues - how to bridge one to the other

1318272167306461191 [2020-10-19] @PrinceVogel 💜 3
Revolutionaries and trads alike should reflect on this. Strip someone of their harmony, and you strip them of the ability to create solidarity, to express rightful desire - and of the potential to wage war. https://t.co/jqqESQfLLA
Images:
  - [Image #0] The image shows a quote from James Connolly's "Introduction to 'Songs of Freedom'", 1907. The quote reads: 
    
    "No revolutionary movement is complete without its poetical expression. If such a movement has caught hold of the imagination of the masses, they will seek a vent in song for the aspirations, the fears and hopes, the loves and hatreds engendered by the struggle. Until the movement is marked by the joyous, defiant, singing of revolutionary songs, it lacks one of the most distinct marks of a popular revolutionary movement; it is a dogma of the few, and not the faith of the multitude."
    
    - James Connolly
    Introduction to "Songs of Freedom", 1907
↓
1318272171765080066 [2020-10-19] @PrinceVogel 💜 3
Musical harmony is an expression of transition between different energetic states. Without graceful transition the costs of changing states is high, and we become stagnant. Stuck in laziness, stuck in work, stuck in the same few notes hammering themselves out over and over again
↓
1318272175141433345 [2020-10-19] @PrinceVogel 💜 3
Whole communities become divided into parties whose political positions are reflections of the only rhythms they know how to occupy - the party of war, the party of leisure.  Only transitioning states under extreme duress, the feeling is of always being off-beat.
↓
1318272176655650819 [2020-10-19] @PrinceVogel 💜 3
Maurice De Saxe, probably the greatest military mind of the 1700s, wrote that music was essential for the long march - pointing out that everyone had the stamina to dance all night if only the music was right.The exhaustion felt today isn't of the body - but the soul.
↓
1318272177779650561 [2020-10-19] @PrinceVogel 💜 3 [(SEED) type=quote_of_root]
When our rhythms are disrupted by cacophony, we cannot coordinate our bodies, or our internal chemistry. Skilled torture strikes at this level - disrupting the sense of day and night, of friend and foe, of noise and silence.https://t.co/VzAEG90fYN
  [Quoting @PrinceVogel: Modern man has had too many experiences.]
↓
1318272179470012417 [2020-10-19] @PrinceVogel 💜 3
For good or ill, the pleasures of the world that "suck you in", offer a resolution of rhythm, an environment where you can have pace and purpose. The dance floor, the dojo, drug addiction, video games, sex - all offer a self-contained context you can "dance" to.
↓
1318272180698959872 [2020-10-19] @PrinceVogel 💜 3
When are they good, when are they bad? Simply, when they provide a foundation for an ever-expanding, ever-lifting harmony, they are good. When they slowly narrow your world, make them the only dance you can dance, they are bad, demonic - the rhythm which insists only on itself.
↓
1318272182284394501 [2020-10-19] @PrinceVogel 💜 3
But when we find rhythms that quiet our own internal storm, we can experience a healing that lets us flourish in more and more of the world. https://t.co/rtpz74TAyP
  [Quoting @PrinceVogel: This video of a dog getting its trauma handled is one of the most informative psychological case studies I've ever seenhttps://t.co/Ug0ttQjMbyWarning: The dog starts out in a pretty rough way, but he gets better in the end]
↓
1318272183509131265 [2020-10-19] @PrinceVogel 💜 4
To find a footing in the modern world, find a history you believe in - a progression of notes that your own life can add to, the harmony you can join. Get anything out of your life that is too much noise, too much part of the storm of disharmony.
